# init inside a git repository with no versioning mode: an exit-2 refusal that
# is self-sufficient — it names the membership of the target and explains what
# each mode does with the repository.

mkdir host
cd host
exec git init -q

exec bash -c 'akb init sub-kb; echo "akb-exit=$?"'
stdout '^akb-exit=2$'
stderr '^usage: sub-kb is inside git repository .* — choose how the KB is versioned:$'
stderr '^  --embed    the KB joins this repository''s history; akb commits only its own paths \(kb/, raw/, \.agent-kb/\), never other worktree changes$'
stderr '^  --no-git   the KB is not versioned; akb excludes it from the host''s git status via \.git/info/exclude \(local to this clone\)$'
# The repo-root layout warning belongs to a target that IS the repository root.
! stderr 'This will write'
! stderr 'internal:'
# The refusal is a preflight: nothing was scaffolded.
! exists sub-kb

# A target nested at any depth gets the same membership wording: it is inside
# the repository, not a repository of its own.
mkdir nested/deeper
cd nested/deeper
exec bash -c 'akb init deep-kb; echo "akb-exit=$?"'
stdout '^akb-exit=2$'
stderr '^usage: deep-kb is inside git repository .* — choose how the KB is versioned:$'
! exists deep-kb
